answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with stake-backed identity. To act on chain, every agent must lock a meaningful bond in escrow. If a challenger proves one operator runs duplicate identities, the protocol slashes that bond, so the attacker loses real capital. Copying an account is free, but each fake still needs its own stake; the operator perches on a narrow ledge of collateral that one challenge knocks away, draining funds like a river and leaving fakes hollow. Every forged identity multiplies the capital at risk, so one more sybil costs more than it earns.
